# About {.unnumbered}

## The notes

*Calculus of Single Variables* is the lecture notes for HMTH101, taught in the Department of Mathematics at the University of Zimbabwe. They were written by **G. Nhawu**, who holds the copyright. The notes cover a first course: the real numbers, functions, sequences, limits and continuity, the derivative and its applications, and integration through to the standard techniques.

They are notes for a taught course, not a textbook. Proofs are given where the course gives them and omitted where it does not, and each chapter ends with the tutorial sheet the class works through.

## This edition

This is a web edition, built by **Donald Zvadah** as a contributor. It is generated from `HMTH101notes.tex`, the same LaTeX source the printed PDFs come from, so the mathematics on this site and the mathematics in the PDFs are the same text.

What the conversion changed:

- **Mathematics is rendered live** by MathJax rather than shown as a page image, so it reflows on a phone, can be selected and copied, and is read correctly by screen readers.
- **Definitions, theorems and corollaries are numbered and addressable.** Each one has its own anchor, so a single result can be linked to directly.
- **Tutorial sheets are boxed** at the end of each chapter, which is the one piece of visual structure the printed notes do not have.
- **One structural repair.** In the printed notes the numbered list of number systems in @sec-basics is never closed, so the remainder of that section prints as part of item 4. On paper this shows only as an indent; on a web page it would swallow five subsections, so the list is closed after the fourth item here.

The wording of the notes is untouched, including the chapter epigraphs and the tutorial questions. No worked solutions have been added.

## Source and corrections

Everything — the LaTeX source, the compiled PDFs, the figures, and the Quarto source for this site — is at [github.com/Donniezvadah/HMTH101-Calculus-1](https://github.com/Donniezvadah/HMTH101-Calculus-1).

Corrections to the web edition, particularly anything where a formula does not match the PDF, are welcome as an issue on that repository. Corrections to the mathematics itself belong with the author.

This is a student project and is not an official University of Zimbabwe publication.
